title: Partial selector maps are wholly unresolvable, not a subset match
context: K8s manifest analysis extracts Service selectors and workload labels to find Service↔workload references. If a selector has any templated value among literal siblings (e.g., `app: {{ .Values.name }}, tier: web`), the whole map must resolve to null—not `{tier: web}` alone. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Any unresolvable (templated) key in a selector/labels map voids the entire map. Partial resolution is forbidden because it is strictly more permissive than the real selector, creating false-positive reference edges. Safety (no false positives) takes priority over coverage (missing real edges when templates are involved).
consequences: Conservative: misses some real edges when manifests contain templated keys mixed with literals
Safe: prevents false-positive Service↔workload edges that would result from incomplete selectors
Requires explicit test coverage to prevent regression (the guard survived mutation until tests were added)
alternatives_rejected: Allow partial maps and use them for matching (creates false-positive edges; strictly wrong)
Attempt to resolve templates statically (out of scope; adds complexity)
Mark partial matches as low-confidence rather than null (still produces spurious edges)
